correctness.rationale: Katsuura Theorem 2 confirms concentric incenter/circumcenter iff equifacial tetrahedron, hence the alternating-sign three-axis disphenoid normal form. Direct face distances show rho^{-2}=alpha^{-2}+beta^{-2}+gamma^{-2}, while R^2=sum squared axes and V=8 alpha beta gamma/3. With positive a,b,c summing to one and Q=sum reciprocals, the cubic z^3-z^2+Q s z-s has discriminant -s(4Q^3s^2-(Q^2+18Q-27)s+4), independently reproduced by exact symbolic computation. Its double-root products give closed V±, while continuity/positive roots fill the interval. Explicit double-root endpoint formulas independently checked at Q=9,10,16,25,100. Q=9 regular; no claim that arbitrary bicentric nonconcentric tetrahedra share the interval.

originality.rationale: Katsuura 2019 fully establishes the equifacial/concentric-center characterization but not the volume spectrum. Gibson–Saldanha–Tomei primary paper describes centered alternating-box tetrahedra and the possible sphere ratio, but its full text provides neither a sharp fixed-(R,rho) volume interval nor both equality shapes. Published disphenoid anisotropy laws control a different fixed statistic. A 1950 isosceles tetrahedron article and older monographs could include hidden volume formulas; retained as residual risk rather than arbitrary rejection. Exact statement-level searches did not identify an implying source.
